summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served at the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and held a professorship at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the École française d'Extrême-Orient, where he served as director as attested in 2003.

François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon and under Pierre Meile and Jean Filliozat. He served as directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1977 to 2002.
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, including as professor as attested in 2008 and 2013.

François Martini was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at INALCO and under Sylvain Lévi. His career included posts at INALCO, the Buddhist Institute (1930–1939), École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer (1946–1960), and EPHE (1957–1965).
François-Marie Bertrand was an Indologist who studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice from around 1826 to 1830 and was a student of Garcin de Tassy.

Françoise L'Hernault was a scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied at INALCO, Annamalai University, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University. In 1971, she joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient to oversee photographic collections.

Françoise Mallison is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She served as directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, succeeding Vaudeville in 1988.

Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at the Sorbonne, INALCO, and the University of Paris. She directed Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine (2001–2011) and served as research director at the CNRS from 2002.
Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied at INALCO under Heather Stoddard. She directed the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental leadership posts at INALCO in 2011 and 2013–2014.

Fred Henry Andrews worked in archaeology and Central Asian studies. His career included serving as curator of the Lahore Museum (1897–1902) and director of the Art Department at Battersea Polytechnic Institute (1902–1920).

Fred Pfeil was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Amherst College and Stanford University. He taught at several institutions, culminating in a teaching post at Trinity College, Hartford from around 1984 to 2005.

Fred Walter Householder, Jr. was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont and Columbia University under Louis H. Gray. He held posts at Allegheny College and Indiana University Bloomington (1948–1983).

Freda Bedi was a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at St Hugh's College (1930–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (1952–1953). She founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.

Frede Møller-Kristensen was an Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He lectured in Pāli at the University of Copenhagen (1966–1972) and directed the Oriental Department at the Royal Danish Library (1969–1987).

Frederic Salmon Growse was an Indologist and historian who studied at Oriel College and The Queen's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1860 to 1891 and was a fellow of the University of Calcutta.
Frederic Spring was an Indologist and linguist who served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society and as a chaplain in the Madras Army until 1824.

Frederick Eden Pargiter was an Indologist educated at Exeter College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1875–1904), as judge of the Calcutta High Court (1904–1906), and as president of The Asiatic Society (1903–1905).

Frederick J. Streng was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy who studied at Texas Lutheran, SMU, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held professorships at USC and SMU (1966–1974).

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist educated at University College London and Trinity Hall. He served as secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910) and editor of the Oxford English Dictionary (1861–1870), founding numerous literary societies.
